question: What is the vitamin deficiency in milk?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Milk is a poor source of Vitamin C.
 
• Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is essential for the repair of tissues and the enzymatic production of certain neurotransmitters.
 
• Human bodies cannot synthesize Vitamin C, thus it must be obtained from the diet.
 
• Common sources of Vitamin C include fruits like oranges, strawberries, kiwi, and vegetables like bell peppers and spinach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin C Deficiency (Scurvy)**

 
 
• Scurvy is a disease resulting from a deficiency of Vitamin C.
 
• Symptoms of scurvy include anemia, debility, exhaustion, spontaneous bleeding, pain in the limbs, and especially the legs, swelling in some parts of the body, and ulceration of the gums and loss of teeth.
 
• Scurvy can be prevented and treated with adequate intake of Vitamin C.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Vitamin C**
 
 
• Vitamin C is important for the biosynthesis of collagen, L-carnitine, and certain neurotransmitters.
 
• It is also involved in protein metabolism.
 
• Vitamin C is a potent antioxidant and helps in the regeneration of other antioxidants within the body.
 
 
 
• **Dietary Sources of Vitamin C**
 
 
• Citrus fruits like oranges, lemons, and grapefruits are rich sources of Vitamin C.
 
• Other fruits such as strawberries, kiwi, and guava also contain high levels of Vitamin C.
 
• Vegetables like bell peppers, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, and spinach are good sources of Vitamin C.
 
 
 
• **Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)**
 
 
• The RDA for Vitamin C varies by age, gender, and life stage.
 
• For example, adult men are recommended to consume 90 mg per day while adult women should consume 75 mg per day.
 
• Smokers are advised to consume an additional 35 mg per day due to the increased oxidative stress from smoking.
